purpose: Public-safe curriculum mapping for Aurora creative tools used by English 9. Tool use supports learning evidence but does not replace assessed mastery.

apps.name: AuraInk
boundaries: Artwork is a composition or observation prompt, not textual evidence.
External template/font dependencies may fail; the blank local canvas must remain a valid fallback.
Student-created visuals used in publication still require accessibility descriptions and editorial review.

apps.name: Aurora Inspiration Game
boundaries: Generated affirmations/prompts are ideation material, not evidence or assessment answers.
Students may reject or modify any generated prompt.
Social-sharing controls are not required for coursework or mastery.

apps.name: Creative Mind Odyssey — Sovereign Edition
boundaries: Prompt output may start thinking but cannot author assessed work for the student.
Saved local responses remain process evidence unless explicitly selected for portfolio use.
Mastery requires the course's defined reading/writing evidence regardless of app score or streak.

apps.name: AuraenTune / Frequency Tuner
potential_language_arts_uses: optional demonstration that pitch/frequency is different from poetic rhythm, meter, stress, and cadence
apps.blocking_issue: Preset descriptions include unsupported wellness/medical-style claims such as restoring cellular balance. Do not present those claims as instructional facts or integrate this app into scored Language Arts work until the public copy is corrected.

global_rules: Aurora tools are optional learning supports unless a lesson explicitly defines an equivalent no-tool pathway.
No Aurora score, streak, artwork, generated prompt, or activity-completion signal may satisfy an 80 percent mastery gate by itself.
Eiren may discuss student-created Aurora work but may not convert it into assessed writing on the student's behalf.
Beta feedback about Aurora integrations remains separate from mastery.
Public-facing curriculum should expose only approved public destinations and educational purpose, never credentials, protected endpoints, repository secrets, internal topology, or network mapping.
